BRANCH_TAKEN: (ii) — AMBIGUOUS. The only arm that moved (B1, -0.1334) moved DOWN, and the adapters were TRAINED at 416x416, so evaluating at 768x768 is a train/test resolution mismatch. Per the pre-registration a decrease licenses ONLY 'not testable without retraining at native resolution' — it does NOT license 'resolution excluded'.
what_can_be_said: the CHAIN arm (V2b) is essentially INSENSITIVE to a 3.4x area resolution change on both accuracy (-0.014) and faithfulness (-0.005)
therefore the chain arms' weak geometry was NOT primarily caused by cell edges unreadable at 416px — the information they failed to use was already present
the CP2 geometry-FABRICATION diagnosis is NOT overturned; the resolution explanation for it is now the LESS likely one
no prior conclusion is retracted on the basis of this audit
what_cannot_be_said: that native resolution would not help a model TRAINED at native resolution — untested
budget_consequence: native prefill 2973 vs 938 tokens/sample (3.17x) TIGHTENS the B1-vs-chain FLOPs ratio from 1.417x to 1.132x, which STRENGTHENS CP1b branch (a): B1's win is measured closer to compute parity at native resolution
actions: annotate all prior perception findings with the effective resolution (416x416, 169 tok/view)
standing effective_resolution field in every future results.json, read from the live processor
any future TRAINING run should use max_pixels>=589824 so the models see the renders E0 validated
cost of native: prefill 938->2973 tok/sample; measured ~3x slower per eval arm

geometry_step_probe.prereg: geometry_step_prereg.md — both candidate sentences written before any number existed
geometry_step_probe.key_comparison: a 3.408x increase in visual information moves the geometry step about as much as, and in no better a direction than, changing the random seed; the mean gain from more pixels (+0.0127) is SMALLER than the mean drift from reseeding (+0.0206)
geometry_step_probe.reading_selected: (b) — insensitivity is itself a fabrication symptom, in the SHARPENED form
geometry_step_probe.prereg_wording_corrected: the pre-registered (ii) wording claimed the output 'never depended on the image'. The per-structure check REFUTES that strong clause: 52.9% of scores change. The defensible claim is that the step is responsive to the image without being INFORMED by it — the changes are symmetric noise.
geometry_step_probe.sentence_to_write: Giving the chain 3.4x more visual information changes its geometry step no more meaningfully than changing the random seed does: 53% of per-structure scores move, but symmetrically (58 up, 53 down, sign-test z=0.47) and with a net effect (+0.013) smaller than seed-to-seed drift (+0.021). The step is responsive to the image without being informed by it — the fabrication signature, and why the CP2 diagnosis survives the resolution audit.
caveats: single seed at native (V2b_s0), single arm
native run is train/test resolution-mismatched (CP0c branch (ii)), which could suppress a real gain
the same-resolution reseed yardstick partly controls for that; a native-TRAINED model is the clean test (queued)

strengthened_reading: both chain checkpoints (V1 pre-GRPO, V2b post-GRPO) are insensitive to the 3.408x area change and V1 even moves slightly UP (+0.0095); the insensitivity is a property of the CHAIN FORMAT reproduced across two independently trained adapters, not an idiosyncrasy of one. Only the DIRECT arm is resolution-sensitive and it moves DOWN — the train/test mismatch signature.
